newsitem.title: USA: Steamboat reopens limited use of Mississippi River.
newsitem.headline: Steamboat reopens limited use of Mississippi River.

text.p: A paddlewheel steamboat with 598 people on board reopened the Mississippi River to one-way traffic Wednesday afternoon after a capsized barge leaking benzene caused the river's closure Monday, the Coast Guard said.

Coast Guard Cmdr. Ken Parris said the American Queen, with 437 passengers and 161 crew members, was allowed to pass the accident scene en route to New Orleans shortly before a Coast Guard marine traffic controller began guiding vessels through. Only one-way traffic, one vessel at a time, is allowed through the area, he said.
More than 20 tows handling an undetermined number of barges and two passenger riverboats were waiting to pass the area where a tow of 25 barges hit a bridge Monday evening.

Two of the barges sank, one was missing, one capsized and the others were quickly rounded up by other tug boats on the river. The capsized tanker barge was carrying a volatile mix of gasoline and benzene, some of which was slowly leaking into the river, authorities said.
As the petrochemicals floated to the surface, a noxious vapour was released. Southern University officials voluntarily evacuated 1,000 students Tuesday night but reopened the campus Wednesday.
Parris said divers were trying late Wednesday to connect hoses underneath the overturned barge to off-load its cargo before using two large cranes brought upriver from New Orleans to right it.
